purpose: Per-passage likelihood contrast between a period-trained causal LM and its modern-trained twin, in bits per UTF-8 byte (period minus modern; negative means the period LM finds the passage easier). Bits per byte keeps models with different tokenizers comparable. Reports mean and median contrast, the share of passages the period LM finds easier, and a seeded bootstrap 95% interval of the mean; with a reference of real period passages it also reports the candidate-minus-reference gap with its own interval. Default pair is talkie-lm 1930 base vs talkie-web base (13B twins, Apache-2.0, custom model code so loading needs --trust-remote-code). The typewriter-ai 1913 7B base declares no license; it loads for private research use with a warning, with a --modern-model of the operator's choice. Rows with precomputed bpb run model-free and --score-cache resumes. Descriptive: not a register verdict and not a reward.
use_when: You want a second, model-likelihood read of how period-like a set of passages is, beside period_ruler
You can run two 7-13B causal LMs (GPU), or already have their bits-per-byte scores
You want to compare generated passages with real period passages on the same two models
do_not_use_when: You want to date a passage or certify its register
You want a training reward (topic and vocabulary move the contrast as much as syntax)
You cannot run 13B models and have no precomputed scores

inputs.reference: optional JSONL of real period passages, same shape
inputs.score_cache: optional JSONL cache of per-model bpb (appended per batch; resumes)

artifacts: results.period_lm_contrast.candidates: mean/median contrast_bpb, bootstrap interval, share_period_easier
results.period_lm_contrast.reference and candidate_minus_reference_* when --reference is given

compute.cost_note: Two causal-LM forward passes per passage (13B twins by default, GPU with ~30 GB or more in bf16); model-free when every row carries precomputed bpb.

examples.description: Talkie twins against a real period reference, caching scores
